title: What you already do
hook: you have a practice already, whether you call it one or not: Nanquan says ordinary mind is the Way, and Zhaozhou pushes back
tomorrow: a prince's father hid every old and sick face. what got past the wall?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: my why. The rabbis said start even for a mixed reason; it can grow into for its own sake. Today, what you're doing already.

Coffee on the back step every morning, the same mug, the same five minutes of watching the street. Is that a practice, or just caffeine? Zen has an old argument about exactly this, between a teacher and his student. The student, Zhaozhou, asks his teacher Nanquan: what is the Way? And Nanquan gives an answer that sounds almost too easy. Ordinary mind is the Way. Your coffee, in other words, might already count. But Zhaozhou isn't satisfied, and his pushback is the real puzzle.
screen: `COFFEE ON THE BACK STEP.` → `WHAT IS THE WAY?` → `ORDINARY MIND IS THE WAY.` → `THE STUDENT PUSHES BACK.`

segments.voice: Should I aim at it, then? Zhaozhou asks. If you aim at it, says Nanquan, you turn away from it. Then Zhaozhou lands his question. If I don't aim at it, how will I know it's the Way? Let both views speak. Nanquan's side: the Way isn't somewhere else, waiting behind a special technique. It's in washing a bowl and walking to work. Chase it as something extra and you've already split your life in two. Zhaozhou's side, and it's strong: if everything already counts, nothing does. A habit you never notice is just a habit. How would you know? Nanquan's answer goes past both. The Way, he says, isn't a matter of knowing or not knowing. Knowing is a kind of illusion, and not knowing is just blankness. Reach it without doubt, and it's open and wide as the sky. The story says Zhaozhou woke up right there. Here's the teaching Zen draws from it: practice isn't only what happens on the cushion. Ordinary mind, awake in ordinary things, is the Way itself. Zen monasteries treat cooking and cleaning as practice too. So your coffee isn't nothing. It's already here. What it lacks, maybe, is you, awake in it.
screen: `IF YOU AIM AT IT, YOU TURN AWAY.` · `HOW WILL I KNOW IT'S THE WAY?` · `NOT KNOWING, NOT NOT KNOWING.` · `ORDINARY MIND, AWAKE.` · then, large: `ALREADY HERE.`

segments.voice: Walk slowly through your home and stop at each place where you already do something every day: the kettle, the sink, the window, the door. At each one, name the habit silently, as if it were already practice. It might be.
What you already do: the habits that are already a practice, in Nanquan's words ordinary mind, waiting for you to be awake in them.
Keep this one: already here, the Way in the ordinary, if you're awake to it. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Zen students study this exchange as case 19 of the Gateless Gate, and Zen monasteries treat daily work, cooking, cleaning and gardening, as part of practice alongside sitting.
